accepted_phrases: Audit all three complete frozen listing bodies and preserve seller attribution. The PS4-compatible third-party listing displays SKU B096TT8TWX, $49.29, 45/100 over 12 reviews, dimensions 7.1 by 4.7 by 2.7 inches, weight 9.1 ounces, refined analog sticks, and seller claims of highly durable ABS, ergonomic grip, precision, and up to eight hours of play. The Xbox-compatible listing displays SKU B08B5YSVJZ, $32.90, 70/100 over 12 reviews, a package measuring 11.22 by 7.2 by 3.9 inches, weight 12 ounces, broad Xbox/PS3/PC compatibility wording, and no headset jack, but its complete body supplies no stick construction, Hall claim, durability test, or repair evidence. The Switch listing displays SKU B08J3ZW8SM, $42.99, 42/100 over 12 reviews, model JC-K, weight 5.6 ounces, package dimensions 5.12 by 4.8 by 1.65 inches, and seller claims of durable ABS, comfort, precision, Switch compatibility, and about ten hours of play. None of the three bodies identifies Hall-effect stick sensing or supplies teardown proof, calibration or dead-zone results, cycle testing, failure denominators, repairability evidence, or multi-year daily-use comparison.

An analog stick translates thumb movement into continuous directional signals, and the frozen overview says many analog sticks use potentiometers. A potentiometer uses a moving wiper against a resistive element and can serve as a joystick position sensor; the general source also notes contamination and long-term reliability concerns for a slider construction. A Hall sensor produces voltage in response to a magnetic-field component and can be used for positioning, while the analog-stick overview describes historical Hall-effect pads and calls them a sturdier alternative. These generic principles explain why contactless position sensing may avoid one class of sliding-contact wear, but they do not prove the construction, calibration, centering, firmware, spring, housing, button, trigger, or overall lifetime of any exact controller. Tribology and wear sources likewise explain friction, wear, gradual material damage, and eventual loss of function without assigning a failure cause or lifetime to any captured product.

Do not rank durability from the three small storefront rating displays, price, seller words such as durable or precision, or the age of a listing. The frozen bodies omit review sampling, authenticity, return denominators, stick-specific failures, usage intensity, and comparable test conditions. The GuliKit forum item is only a headline claiming drift-free Hall-effect joysticks for a handheld console upgrade kit; it is not a complete-controller teardown, an independent longevity test, or evidence about the three listed controllers. One post depicts severe drift and replacement, and another reports two PS5 controllers failing within three months, but neither provides a controlled denominator, verified cause, exact usage profile, or cross-model comparison. These anecdotes establish that users can experience drift and value replacement, not a population failure rate or a durable winner.

Before checkout, verify the buyer's exact platform and games, the exact controller model and revision, native or adapter-based compatibility, wired or wireless requirements, headset and other required features, seller identity, current checkout price, warranty and return path. Obtain model-bound evidence for the stick sensor and mechanical construction, calibration and dead-zone behavior, firmware update path, replaceable modules or parts, teardown/serviceability, cycle or endurance testing with method and sample size, failure and return denominators, and longitudinal daily-use results. Separate a Hall-stick claim from proof of the rest of the controller and check centering, spring, housing, buttons, triggers, battery, connection, and repair path. If an urgent compatible controller is bought without durability proof, treat it as a provisional purchase under a strong return policy rather than the demonstrated long-life winner.

The three frozen product listings are not interchangeable alternatives: one is sold as a third-party PS4 replacement with PC and mobile claims, one as an Xbox/PS3/PC controller, and one as a Switch controller. A displayed price or rating cannot rescue an option that does not support the buyer's actual platform, games, connection method, or required features. Platform, revision, adapter needs, input support, headset needs, and return conditions must therefore be resolved before any product comparison or purchase recommendation.

No frozen source proves that any of the three listed controllers uses Hall-effect sensing or is a multi-year durability winner, and the listings target different platform sets. The evidence-bounded action is to defer the long-life recommendation and purchase until the buyer's platform is fixed and an exact compatible model has model-bound sensor, calibration, construction, repairability, endurance, failure-denominator, and longitudinal evidence. The Hall mechanism is a relevant screening feature but not a whole-controller lifetime guarantee; storefront ratings, prices, seller adjectives, one upgrade-kit headline, and individual drift posts cannot replace comparative durability evidence. If an immediate replacement is unavoidable, choose only an actually compatible model with a verifiable return or warranty path and label the choice provisional, not proven durable.

Defer the long-life controller purchase until the platform and an exact compatible model's Hall implementation, calibration, construction, repairability, endurance, failure denominators, and longitudinal daily-use evidence are verified.
No frozen product is a proven multi-year durability winner, so defer rather than selecting from ratings, seller claims, headlines, or anecdotes.
The Xbox-compatible controller is the longest-lasting choice because its 70/100 storefront rating is the highest.
The PS4-compatible controller is the durability winner because it is the most expensive frozen listing.
Seller claims such as highly durable ABS, precision control, or ergonomic comfort independently prove multi-year stick durability.
The generic Hall-effect sensor definition proves that one or more of the three frozen controller listings uses Hall-effect sticks.
The GuliKit upgrade-kit headline proves that any of the three complete controllers is drift-free or long-lived.
The two individual drift posts establish a controller population failure rate or a controlled cross-model durability ranking.
The tribology, wear, or potentiometer overview proves the exact failure cause and lifetime of a captured controller.
The PS4, Xbox, and Switch controller listings are interchangeable choices regardless of the buyer's platform and games.
A Hall-stick label by itself guarantees the controller's centering, firmware, springs, buttons, triggers, battery, connection, and multi-year lifetime.
The frozen corpus proves one unconditional controller winner that should be bought now for years of daily play.

research_subgoals.description: Build the complete three-listing matrix with exact price and rating displays, SKU or model, platform wording, physical and feature claims, and every absent Hall, teardown, calibration, endurance, denominator, repairability, and longitudinal measurement.
Explain analog-stick, potentiometer, Hall-sensor, tribology, and wear mechanisms while preserving the boundary between generic plausibility and exact-model implementation, cause, or lifetime.

Scope the storefront ratings, price, seller wording, GuliKit upgrade-kit headline, and two individual failure posts without turning them into failure rates, independent tests, transferable construction claims, or a product ranking.

Apply the platform hard gate and specify an exact-model preflight for revision, games, connection and features, sensor construction, calibration, firmware, serviceability, endurance methods and sample size, failure denominators, longitudinal use, warranty, return, and replacement parts.

Choose an exact controller only if the evidence establishes compatible multi-year durability; otherwise defer, and describe the narrowly provisional urgent-purchase path without mislabeling it as a proven long-life winner.

query_requirements.text: Audit every complete frozen product body for exact price and rating displays, SKU or model, platform and feature wording, physical details, seller durability claims, and missing Hall, teardown, calibration, endurance, denominator, repairability, and longitudinal evidence.

Explain the analog-stick, potentiometer, Hall-sensor, tribology, and wear evidence and state exactly why generic mechanism evidence cannot establish any captured product's sensor construction, failure cause, or lifetime.

Evaluate what the storefront ratings, prices, seller adjectives, GuliKit upgrade-kit headline, and two drift reports can and cannot show about implementation, prevalence, causality, and comparative durability.

Apply exact platform compatibility before price or durability ranking, then give a purchase preflight covering model and revision, games and connection, required features, Hall implementation, calibration, firmware, repairability, endurance method and sample, failure denominators, longitudinal daily use, warranty, returns, and parts.

Recommend an exact proven-compatible controller, a narrowly provisional urgent replacement, or deferral. Preserve every platform, rating, seller, mechanism, upgrade-kit, anecdote, endurance, repair, and missing-evidence boundary and state what new evidence would change the decision.
